# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — basic-economy over-refusal + change-pricing + payment errors (first pass off seed)
- Changes I made:
  - policy.md "Change flights": narrowed "basic economy flights cannot be modified" to mean SEGMENT changes only; added 2 worked examples that cabin/passenger/baggage changes ARE allowed on basic economy. [cluster 1: tasks 17, 22]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_flights`: in-body guard raises only when current cabin==basic_economy AND the (flight_number,date) set changes (cabin-only change allowed) — deterministic boundary for the loosened prompt. [cluster 1]
  - tools.py new READ tool `get_reservation_flights_update_price`: returns num_passengers + amount_due for a proposed cabin/flight change from live DB (×passengers). [cluster 2: tasks 12, 37]
  - policy.md "Change cabin": cabin is all-or-nothing across passengers; price = per-pax diff × num passengers; call the preview tool + STATE the exact figure; downgrade refunds the DIFFERENCE (not full fare); don't cancel a requested downgrade. [clusters 2 & 4: tasks 12, 37, 11]
  - tools.py `book_reservation` payment_methods docstring + policy Payment note: exact `{"payment_id","amount"}` shape, forbid `id/type/source`, amounts must sum to system total. [cluster 3: task 23]
  - tools.py `book_reservation` sum check: enriched actionable error (computed total, provided sum, exact delta to adjust). [cluster 3: task 23]
- Expected effect + why safe: fixes over-refusal (17,22) by teaching the true basic-economy boundary and enforcing it in code; gives the correct change price (12,37) and pushes communicating it; unblocks the payment loop (23). All bounded: the guard fires only on basic-economy segment swaps, the enriched error only on an existing mismatch, the quote tool is read-only, doc/prompt additions are additive/narrowing. Passing tasks 8 & 25 (books that already add up, correct payment shape), 19 (basic-economy return-flight change → still forbidden → cancel unchanged), 40 (passenger rename) are untouched.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration off the seed baseline (LEDGER/RUNMAP empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 37 exact gold (gold has 2 search_direct_flight the agent skipped — may require searching business availability before upgrade); task 11 DB flip (agent followed an explicit "cancel" instruction vs gold downgrade) and task 12 budget decision both still depend on agent reasoning after the new pricing inputs.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if 12/37/11 remain, consider a composite atomic WRITE tool that performs "quote → confirm-cost-fits → update" so the budget/decision logic is enforced in code rather than left to the model; and inspect whether task 37 gold requires a business-availability search step.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.500 Δ=+0.100 · fixed={11, 12, 22} · broke={19, 8}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

## Iteration cand_0002 — re-capture the SAFE cand_0001 wins (pricing) + a 19-preserving basic-economy fix + task-37 card fix; DROP the two regressing edits
- Changes I made (1 line/edit):
  - tools.py NEW READ tool `get_reservation_flights_update_price` — computes amount_due = (per-pax fare diff × num_passengers) from live prices; +ve=pay, −ve=refund the difference. [clusters 12, 11]
  - tools.py in-body guard in `update_reservation_flights` — raises ONLY when cabin==basic_economy AND the (flight_number,date) segment set changes (cabin-only change allowed). [cluster 17/22; bounded enforcement + protects 19's segment-change class]
  - policy.md "Change flights" — narrowed "basic economy cannot be modified" to SEGMENTS-only; 2 worked examples (ALLOWED cabin-upgrade-same-flights; NOT-allowed segment-change → offer cancel). NO anti-cancel prose. [cluster 17/22]
  - policy.md "Change cabin" — cabin is all-or-nothing across passengers; price = per-pax diff × N; call the preview tool + STATE the figure; downgrade refunds the DIFFERENCE (not full fare) and does NOT cancel. [clusters 12, 11]
  - policy.md "Modify flight → Payment" — use the card the user NAMES (match by last_four); don't default to the card on the reservation. [cluster 37]
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - 17/22 fixed by teaching the true basic-economy boundary so the agent performs the cabin+passenger+baggage changes; SAFE because segment changes stay forbidden (guard + example) and I removed the anti-cancel language, so task 19 still cancels and task 40's passenger change still works.
  - 12 fixed: preview tool returns amount_due=1200>$650 → agent declines upgrade, adds bags only. 11 fixed: preview returns −5244 → agent downgrades via update_reservation_flights, refunds $5244, doesn't cancel. SAFE: read-only tool + cabin-change prompt rules that no passing task's trajectory touches.
  - 37 fixed: agent maps "card ending 7334"→credit_card_9074831 and passes it → payment_history matches gold. SAFE: additive attention rule; no passing task selects a differing change-payment card.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 (REJECTED, fixed {11,12,22}, broke {19,8}). I RE-INTRODUCED the SAFE parts (pricing preview tool + pricing/downgrade prompt that fixed 11/12) and a narrower basic-economy fix. I did NOT re-try (a) the "do not cancel-and-rebook / don't cancel unless explicitly asked" prose — it regressed task 19; (b) the book_reservation payment_methods docstring rewrite — it regressed task 8 AND did not fix 23, so book_reservation is UNTOUCHED this iteration.
- Refuted hypotheses (do NOT re-test): loosening the basic-economy rule with imperative anti-cancel prose breaks task 19; rewriting book_reservation's payment docstring breaks task 8.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 23 (multi-booking behavioral stall — executed 2 of 3 bookings, hallucinated the 3rd). Design NOT yet tried: a composite/loop tool over book_reservation that delegates per-item (DB-identical for single bookings 8/25) and is the only booking path, forcing all 3 writes. Deferred this iteration because any change to the book_reservation write path risks passing 8/25 (cand_0001 proved book_reservation edits regress 8).
- Plateau signal: only 1 accepted-vs-rejected data point so far (cand_0001 rejected). Lever choice this iteration = bounded code (guard + read compute tool) + tightly-scoped additive prompt, explicitly avoiding the two prompt edits that regressed.
- Focus next iteration: if this is accepted, tackle task 23 with a delegating book_reservations loop tool (add → verify DB-identical on 8/25 → then consider swap). If 17/22 still fail, the basic-economy KNOWLEDGE fix may need reinforcing; if 19 regresses again, the basic-economy prompt narrowing itself is the culprit → move it entirely into a code guard and revert the prompt text.
